Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 20, verse 108:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day they will follow the caller, with no deviation from him﴾

That is, they will accept from every direction the call of his voice and his side, not turning away from him.

Al-Farra' said: This is like when you say, "I called you with a call, with no deviation from it for you."

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is "there is no deviation for them from his call," i.e., they are unable to do anything but follow him and head toward him.

If you say: If the meaning is "there is no deviation for them from my call," how does He say "no deviation for him"?

It is said: A group said the lam here means "from," i.e., "no deviation from him."

Another group said the meaning is "there is no deviation for them from my call," as al-Zajjaj said.

Both opinions involve evident strain. Since the call reaches all of them without deviating from them, and all of them head toward the caller's voice and follow it without deviating from it, the use of the lam fits both meanings and indicates them both.

The meaning is: there is no deviation in his call, neither in its reaching them nor in their answering it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾

That is: they became silent, subdued, and humbled. From this comes the description of the earth as "khushu'" (humbled), which is its dryness and lowness, and its not being raised by rain and vegetation. He, exalted, says: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾ [Fussilat: 39].

Khushu' (humble submissiveness): the heart standing before the Lord in submission, humiliation, and gathering of itself upon Him.

It is also said: khushu' is submission to the truth, and this is among the requirements of khushu'.

Among its signs: when a servant is opposed and is corrected with the truth, he receives that with acceptance and submission.

The commentary on the pronoun in ﴿به﴾ (“by it” / “of Him”) has been disputed. It has been said that it refers to Allah, the Exalted, meaning: and they do not encompass Him in knowledge.

It has also been said that it refers to what is before them and behind them, so that according to the first view the pronoun returns to the Knower (al-ʿālim), and according to the second it returns to the known (al-maʿlūm).

This second view entails the first, but not vice versa, because if they do not encompass some of the things known to them that relate to them, then not encompassing Him, the Exalted, in knowledge is all the more so.

It means: he will not have added to him any of the evil deeds of what he did not do, nor will any of the good deeds of what he did be diminished. And if injustice were the impossible thing that cannot exist, then the absence of fear of it would have no meaning, and security from its occurrence would have no benefit.

(Section)

Scholars have differed about what the exception (*istithna'*, a grammatical construction that removes part of a general statement) excludes. Al-Kisa'i held that it excludes only from the stated term (*al-mustathna minhu*), which is the thing about which the judgement is made. So when you say, "The people came except Zayd," Zayd is excluded from "the people," as though you had reported that the people among whom there is no Zayd came. As for Zayd himself, you have reported nothing about him. You have withheld any report about him, rather than reporting the negation of coming about him. The difference between the two is clear. On his view, the predication occurs after the exclusion.

Al-Farra' held that it excludes from the ruling itself. Most scholars held that it excludes from both together. The exception therefore has two aspects. The first is that it is excepted, and in this respect it is excluded from the stated noun. The second is that it is the subject of a judgement opposite to the ruling on the stated term, and in this respect it is excluded from that ruling. The correct view is that it is excluded from a noun qualified by the ruling. It is therefore excluded from a restricted noun, not from an unrestricted one.

Here we mention the arguments advanced for these positions and the objections raised against those arguments. Al-Kisa'i argued from the words of God Most High: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused.﴾

The basis of his inference is this: if the exception excluded from the ruling, then the words "he refused" would be redundant, since that is already known from the exception.

This was answered by saying that it is emphasis.

This answer was objected to on the grounds that the meanings conveyed by particles are not emphasized. One does not say "Zayd did not stand" with negation emphasized, or "Did Amr stand?" with interrogation emphasized, or "But Zayd stood" with contrast emphasized, and the like. This is because the particle was placed for brevity, which is why one turns from the verb to it. Emphasizing it with a verb contradicts the purpose for which it was placed.

The correct answer is that "he refused" conveys an additional meaning: his failure to prostrate is attributed to his refusal, which is an existing attribute he possessed and from which the sin arose. His failure to prostrate was therefore not due to incapacity, nor to forgetfulness, nor to heedlessness, but was refusal and arrogance. It is known that this is not understood from the exception alone. What the exception conveys is only his non-prostration. As for what motivated his non-prostration, the exception does not indicate it, so it was stated explicitly.

The same argument, objection and reasoning apply exactly to His words: ﴿Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis. He was not among those who prostrate.﴾

The negation of his being among the prostrators is more specific than the negation of prostration from him. Negating his being among them implies negating his fitness and readiness, so it is more forceful in blame than saying only that he did not prostrate.

Several points show the invalidity of this position. Among them: if what follows "illa" were silence about its ruling, then "There is no god but God" would not be a declaration of monotheism. The consequent is false, so the antecedent is false too. Both premises are evident.

Among them: the disconnected exception (*al-istithna' al-munqati'*) does not allow exclusion from the noun, since the excepted item is not included in it. The same should hold for the connected exception.

Among them: if exclusion were from the noun alone, it would not be valid to make an exception from the content of a sentence, as when you say, "Zayd is your brother, except that he is far from you," or "Amr is your friend, except that he loves your enemy," and the like.

Among them: no such usage occurs in Arabic speech as "The people stood, except Zayd, who stood." For if exclusion were from the noun alone and the excepted were left unstated, it would be permissible to affirm standing for him just as it is permissible to negate it. Silence about his ruling neither indicates the negation of standing nor its affirmation, so neither would contradict the exception.

When the invalidity of the two positions is clear, the position that exclusion is from the ruling and not from the noun is sound.

The same holds for the whole category. What has been answered to this is that the excepted item is included, by estimation, with the noun subject to the judgement, since the first term is conceived as general in some respect so that the exception is valid. The advocate of al-Kisa'i's view may also give this answer.

When the invalidity of the two positions is clear, the position of the majority is sound: exclusion is from the noun and the ruling together. The excepted noun is excluded from the stated term, and its ruling is excluded from the ruling of that term. What is impossible is to exclude the excepted noun from the stated term while it is included under it in the ruling. In that case exclusion is not conceivable at all. If it shared the same ruling, it would enter with the term in both the ruling and the noun, and its exception would be unintelligible.

It is not said that the meaning of the exception is that the speaker abstains from reporting about the excepted item, either by negation or by affirmation, while each remains possible. We reply that this is false for many reasons.

Among them: when you say, "Nothing stood except Zayd," "I struck none except Amr," or "I passed by none except Zayd," and similar exceptions with no stated subject (*al-istithna'at al-mufarraghat*), no one doubts that you affirm these rulings for what follows "illa," just as you negate them from others. Indeed, affirming them for the excepted is stronger than negating them from others.

Whoever says the ruling on the excepted item is left unstated must accept that standing, striking and passing are not understood to be affirmed for Zayd from these sentences. That is certainly false.

Among them: if the excepted item were left unstated, a man would not enter Islam by saying "There is no god but God," because on that false assumption he would not have affirmed divinity for God. Yet this is the greatest formula, which by its form includes the negation of divinity from everything other than God and the affirmation of it for Him by exclusivity. Its indication of affirmation is therefore greater than that of our saying "God is a god." No one doubts this at all.

Among them: if someone claims against a man a hundred dirhams, and he replies, "I owe you a hundred, less three dirhams," he thereby denies that the three dirhams are owed to the claimant. If he were silent about them, he would have confessed to part and refrained from answering about part. No sensible person says this. If the ruling on the excepted item were silence, he would be one who refrains from answering.

Among them: what people of discourse understand from this is the negation of the ruling from the excepted item and its affirmation for the stated term. For them there is no difference at all between understanding this negation and understanding that affirmation. This is in their usage like understanding commands, prohibitions, negation, interrogation and the other meanings of speech. So no listener understands from the words of God Most High: ﴿He remained among them a thousand years, less fifty years﴾ that He reported about nine hundred and fifty years and was silent about the fifty, reporting nothing about them. No one ever understands otherwise than that he did not remain among them for those fifty years.

Likewise His words: ﴿[Iblis] said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them."﴾ Nothing is understood from this except that the sincere servants cannot be led astray by him. The same applies to all other exceptions.

Among them: when the speaker says, "The people stood, except Zayd," his speech is not truthful unless the people stood and Zayd did not. That is why whoever wants to refute him says, "You lied; rather Zayd stood." If Zayd were left unstated, this would not be a refutation, yet all sensible people count it as one and count his report as false, since they count reporting contrary to what is the case as lying.

When this is understood, the difficulty raised by some later scholars about the exception is resolved. They said: "The exception is hard to conceive. For when you say, 'The people came except Zayd,' either Zayd is included among the people or he is not. If he is not included, the exception is not sound, since it is exclusion, and excluding what was never included is not conceivable. If he is included, his exclusion is not sound, because it contradicts itself, since you judge him by two contradictory rulings."

Because of this difficulty, al-Qadi and his followers said: "'Ten except three' is synonymous with 'seven.' They are two nouns combined with a particle and placed for this number." If al-Qadi meant that the meaning understood from them is one, this is correct. If he meant grammatical composition, it is false.

The answer to this difficulty is that a judgement of predication is not made until the simple terms have been fully stated, since predication occurs only after the exclusion. The speaker who says, "The people stood, except Zayd," has here five things. First, standing as a simple term. Second, the people as a simple term. Third, Zayd as a simple term. Fourth, the relation between the two terms. Fifth, the particle indicating the negation of the relation from Zayd.

So Zayd is included among the people on the supposition of no predication, and excluded from them on the supposition of predication. Predication occurs after his exclusion. His inclusion and his exclusion are therefore by two different considerations that do not contradict each other. He is included by considering the individual terms and excluded by considering the relation. So he is one of the people, but not one of the people who are the subject of the ruling. This is the clarification of this difficulty and its resolution, and God is the One who grants success.

**(Benefit)**

**[Section: The difference between *ihtiyat* (caution) and *waswasa* (obsessive scrupulosity)]**

The difference between *ihtiyat* (precautionary caution) and *waswasa* (obsessive scrupulosity) is this: *ihtiyat* is thoroughness and earnestness in following the Sunnah and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions practised, without excess, transgression, negligence or neglect. This is the caution that Allah and His Messenger are pleased with. As for *waswasa*, it is the innovation of what the Sunnah has not brought and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and none of the Companions did, while claiming that by it one reaches the attainment and mastery of what is prescribed. Such a person, in his own view, is being cautious: he washes his limbs in wudu more than three times, so he wastes water in pouring it during his ablution and ritual bath; he repeatedly or once pronounces the intention for prayer aloud; he washes his clothes of what he is not certain is impure, out of caution; and he refrains from praying in his shoes, out of caution. These, and many times more than these, are what the obsessive have taken as religion, claiming them to be caution. Yet caution lies in following the guidance of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he practised, and that is more fitting for them, for it is the caution which whoever departs from has parted from caution and deviated from the even path. Complete caution lies in avoiding opposition to the Sunnah, even if one opposes most of the people of the earth, indeed all of them.

**(Subtle point)**

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then His Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him.﴾

The accursed one, out of his ignorance, supposed that Allah, glorified is He, would forsake His chosen and beloved, whom He created with His own hand, into whom He breathed of His spirit, to whom He caused His angels to prostrate, and whom He taught the names of all things, on account of a single meal he ate.

He did not know that a physician teaches the patient the remedy before the illness. When the patient feels the illness, he hastens to use the remedy. Likewise, when an enemy shoots him with an arrow that strikes not a fatal spot, he hastens to treat the wound, and he stands up as though no harm had befallen him.

The enemy was afflicted with sin, and he persisted, argued, opposed the command, found fault with the wisdom, did not ask for pardon, and did not repent of his lapse. The Beloved was afflicted with sin, and he acknowledged it, repented, was remorseful, humbled himself, submitted, and resorted to the refuge of creation, which is monotheism and seeking forgiveness. So the reproach was removed from him, his sin was forgiven, his repentance was accepted, and every door of mercy and guidance was opened to him. We are his children, and whoever resembles his father has not been wronged. Whoever's disposition is repentance and seeking forgiveness has been guided to the finest of dispositions.

**(Benefit)**

As for the Most High's words in Surah Taha: ﴿He said: "Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others."﴾ This is addressed to Adam and Eve.

Some scholars have said that the pronoun in His words ﴿Go down from it﴾ may refer either to Adam and his wife, or to Adam and Iblis. The wife is not mentioned because she follows him. On this view, the enmity mentioned is between the two addressed by the descent, namely Adam and Iblis, and the matter is clear.

On the first view, the verse contains two matters:

The first: His command, exalted is He, to Adam and his spouse to descend.

The second: His information about the enmity between Adam and his wife on one side and Iblis on the other. This is why the plural pronoun is used in the second matter and not in the first. It is certain that Iblis is included in the ruling of this enmity, as the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife﴾, and He said to the descendants: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾.

Reflect on how the passages mentioning enmity all use the plural pronoun rather than the dual.

As for the descent, He mentions it sometimes with the plural, sometimes with the dual, and sometimes with the singular, as in His words in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿He said: "Go down from it"﴾. Likewise in Surah Sad, and that was addressed to Iblis alone.

Wherever it occurs in the plural form, it addresses Adam, his wife and Iblis, since the story revolves around them. Wherever it occurs in the dual, it either addresses Adam and his wife, since they are the two who actually ate from the tree and committed the disobedience, or it addresses Adam and Iblis, since they are the fathers of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn) and the origins of the descendants. Thus their situation and the outcome of their affair are mentioned as an admonition and lesson for their offspring. Both views have been related.

What clarifies that the pronoun in His words ﴿Go down from it, all of you﴾ refers to Adam and Iblis is that when Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the disobedience, He singled out Adam without his wife, saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him. He said: "Go down from it, all of you"﴾.

This shows that the one addressed by the descent is Adam and the one who made disobedience appealing to him, and the wife entered as a follower. For the purpose is that Allah, exalted is He, informs the two weighty ones of what befell their two progenitors from the ill omen of disobedience and opposition to the command. Mentioning their two fathers conveys this meaning more forcefully than mentioning only the two fathers of mankind.

He, glorified is He, has informed us that the wife ate with Adam, and He informed us that He sent him down and expelled him from the Garden because of that eating. So it is known that the wife's ruling is the same and that she came to the same state as Adam. Directing attention to the situation of the two fathers of the two weighty ones is more fitting than directing it only to the father and mother of mankind. Reflect on this.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.﴾

He negated from him going astray, which is the torment of the heart and spirit, and suffering, which is the torment of the body and spirit as well. So he is granted delight of heart and body through guidance and success.

**(Benefit)**

Know that it has been established in His wisdom, glorified is He, that happiness, bliss and comfort are reached only over the bridge of hardship and fatigue, and entered only through the gate of hardships, patience and bearing toils. For this reason He surrounded Paradise with hardships and the Fire with desires. And for this reason He expelled His chosen, Adam, from Paradise, though He had created it for him. His wisdom required that he not enter it in a lasting entry except after toil and weariness. So He expelled him from it only so that He might admit him into it in the most complete entry.

How great is the difference between the first entry and the second entry! And how great is the difference between the Prophet's entry into Mecca under the protection of al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi and his entry into it on the day of the Conquest!

How great is the difference between the comfort and delight of the believers in Paradise after enduring what came before, and their delight had they been created in it!

How great is the difference between the joy of one whom He grants wellbeing after his trial, enriches after his poverty, guides after his straying, and gathers his heart after its dispersion, and the joy of one who has never tasted those bitternesses! The divine wisdom has already decreed that hardships are causes of pleasures and goods, as the Most High said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, and it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing which is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing which is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾

*A verse of poetry:*
"Often what is hateful to the souls becomes
the cause of what they love, and its like is no cause."

**(Section: On the mention of the dispute between Adam and Musa, peace be upon them)**

In this matter the Prophet (ﷺ) judged in favour of Adam, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

From Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Adam and Musa argued. Musa said: 'O Adam, you are our father; you made us miserable and expelled us from the Garden.' Adam said to him: 'You are Musa, whom Allah chose by His speech, and He inscribed the Torah for you with His own hand. Do you blame me for a matter that Allah decreed for me before He created me by forty years?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'So Adam won the argument over Musa, so Adam won the argument over Musa, so Adam won the argument over Musa.'"

In another narration: "He inscribed the Torah for you with His own hand."

In another wording: "Adam and Musa disputed. Musa said to him: 'You are Adam, whom you led people astray and expelled them from the Garden.' Adam said: 'You are Musa, whom Allah gave the knowledge of all things and chose above the people with His message.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you blame me for a matter that was decreed upon me before I was created?'"

In another wording: "Adam and Musa argued before their Lord. Adam won the argument over Musa. Musa said: 'You are Adam, whom Allah created with His hand, breathed into you of His spirit, caused His angels to prostrate to you, settled you in His Garden, then you caused the people to descend to the earth because of your sin.' Adam said: 'You are Musa, whom Allah chose with His message and His speech, gave you the tablets in which is the clarification of everything, and brought you near as a confidant. How much before my creation did you find Allah had written the Torah?' Musa said: 'Forty years.' Adam said: 'Did you find in it: "And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray"?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you blame me for doing an action that Allah wrote that I should do before He created me by forty years?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'So Adam won the argument over Musa.'"

In another wording: "Adam and Musa argued. Musa said to him: 'You are the one whose sin expelled us from the Garden.'" And he mentioned the hadith...

It is agreed upon as authentic, and this determination occurred after the earlier determination mentioned before, by fifty thousand years before the creation of the heavens.

The Mu'tazilites who failed to understand this hadith rejected it, such as Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i and those who agreed with him. He said: "If it were authentic, the prophethoods of the prophets would be invalidated, for if predestination were a proof for the disobedient, the command and prohibition would be void. For the one who disobeys by abandoning a command or committing a prohibition, if the argument from predestination is valid for him, blame is lifted from him."

This is from the error of the Mu'tazilite group and their ignorance of Allah, His Messenger and his Sunnah. This is an authentic hadith, agreed upon as authentic, which the Umma has never ceased to receive with acceptance from the time of its Prophet, generation after generation, meeting it with affirmation and submission. The people of hadith recorded it in their books and bore witness that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it, and they judged it authentic. What then is the matter with those most ignorant of the Sunnah, and those known for their enmity to it and to its bearers, and for testifying against them that they are anthropomorphists, likeners and literalist filler-transmitters? This has been the way of the people of false kalam (theology), who have always been charged with rejecting the hadiths of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that contradict their false principles and corrupt creeds. They rejected the hadiths of the vision (of Allah), the hadiths of Allah's elevation above His creation, the hadiths of His attributes subsisting in Him, the hadiths of intercession, the hadiths of His descent to the lowest heaven, His descent to the earth to judge between His servants, the hadiths of His speaking by revelation as real speech that whomever He wills of His creation hears, and similar matters. Likewise the Kharijites and Mu'tazilites rejected the hadiths about the emergence of the people of major sins from the Fire through intercession and other things. The Rafidites rejected the hadiths about the virtues of the rightly-guided Caliphs and other Companions. The Mu'attilah (deniers of attributes) rejected the hadiths of the attributes and voluntary actions. The Qadariyyah, who are the Magians of this Umma, rejected the hadiths of decree and predestination. Every one who established a principle that Allah and His Messenger did not establish has been driven by compulsion to reject the Sunnah and distort it from its proper places. Therefore the party of Allah and His Messenger has established no principle other than what the Messenger brought. It is their foundation upon which they rely, and their paradise to which they return.

Then people differed in understanding this hadith and the aspect of the argument by which Adam prevailed over Musa.

One group said: "He prevailed over him only because Adam was his father, so he prevailed over him as a man prevails over his son." This statement has no substance whatsoever, for Allah's proof must be turned to whether the one involved is a father or a son, a slave or a master. Even if a man prevails over his father with a true proof, it is obligatory to yield to the proof.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because the sin was under one law and the blame under another law."

This is of the same type as the previous view, for this has no influence on the argument in any way. This Umma blames the nations that opposed their earlier messengers, even though they did not share one law, and Allah accepts their testimony against them even though they were not people of the same law.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because he had repented of the sin, and the one who has repented of sin is like one who has no sin, and it is not permissible to blame him." Although this is closer than what preceded it, it is not valid, for three reasons:

First: Adam did not mention this aspect, nor did he make it a proof against Musa. He did not say: "Do you blame me for a sin from which I have repented?"

Second: Musa knows Allah, glorified is He, and His command and religion better than to blame a sin about which Allah informed him that He had forgiven its doer, chose him afterwards, and guided him. This is not permissible even for ordinary believers, let alone the interlocutor of the Most Merciful.

Third: This would entail nullifying what the Prophet (ﷺ) attached as the aspect of the argument, and taking into account what he set aside, which should not be considered.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because Musa blamed him in a realm that is not the abode of obligation. If he had blamed him in the abode of obligation, the argument would have been Musa's." This too is invalid for two reasons:

First: Adam did not say to him: "You blamed me in a realm that is not the abode of obligation." He said only: "Do you blame me for a matter decreed for me before I was created?" He did not address the realm; he argued from the prior decree.

Second: Allah, glorified is He, blames the blameworthy among His servants in a realm that is not the abode of obligation. He blames them after death and blames them on the Day of Resurrection.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because Adam witnessed the divine judgment and its operation over creation, and the Lord's sole lordship, and that not a particle moves except by His will and knowledge, that none can repel His decree and destiny, and that what He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be." They said: "The servant's witnessing of the judgment leaves him no room to find any evil reprehensible, for he sees himself as pure nonexistence, the judgments operate upon him, he knows them, and he is subjugated, a created and managed being with no strategy and no power. Whoever witnesses this station is relieved of blame." This path is the most corrupt path that has been taken in this hadith, and it is worse than the path of the Qadariyyah in rejecting it. They rejected it only to refute this claim and to answer its proponents. They were right in their refutation of these people and in demolishing their claim, but they erred in rejecting the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For if this path were valid, all religions would be nullified altogether, predestination would become a proof for every polytheist, disbeliever and wrongdoer, the prescribed punishments would have no meaning, no criminal would be blamed for his crime, no wrongdoer for his wrongdoing, and no one would ever forbid wrongdoing.

For this reason the shaykh of the heretics, Ibn Sina, said in his *Isharat*: "The gnostic does not forbid wrongdoing, because he has insight into the secret of Allah in predestination." This is words stripped of religion and of following the messengers. Allah's most knowing creatures of Him are His messengers and prophets, and they are the greatest of people in forbidding wrongdoing. They were sent only to forbid wrongdoing. So the gnostic is the greatest of people in forbidding wrongdoing, because of his insight into the command and the decree. The command obliges him to forbid, and the decree helps him in it and enacts it for him. So he stands in the station of "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help" and in the station of "So worship Him and rely upon Him." We worship Him by His command and His decree, and we rely on Him in executing His command by His decree. This is the reality of knowledge, and the possessor of this station is the gnostic of Allah. Upon this all the messengers agreed, from the first to the last.

As for the one who says:
"I have become one acted upon by what He chooses from me, so my every act is obedience,"
and who says: "Even if I disobey His command, I have obeyed His will and His wish," and who says: "The gnostic does not forbid wrongdoing, because of his insight into Allah's secret in predestination," such a person has departed from what all the messengers were upon, and he is not among their followers. Allah, glorified is He, related the argument from predestination of the polytheists, the enemies of the messengers, saying: ﴿Those who associated partners with Allah will say: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers"﴾ up to His words: ﴿Say: "Then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof. So had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ And He said: ﴿Those who associated partners said: "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, we or our fathers"﴾ up to His words: ﴿So is there upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ And He said: ﴿And when it is said to them: "Spend from what Allah has provided you," those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?"﴾ And He said: ﴿And they say: "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾

These are four places in which the argument from predestination is related from His enemies. Their shaykh and imam in this was their most despicable enemy, Iblis, who argued against Allah by His decree, saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make [evil] attractive to them upon the earth and will mislead them all."﴾

If it is said: The texts and reason have established the truth of their words, "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor our fathers," and "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him," and "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them," for what Allah wills comes to be and what He does not will does not come to be. And the Most High said: ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾, and He said: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾.

Then how could I call them liars, when He denied them knowledge and affirmed that they were only guessing, while they are truthful in what they claim? All the People of the Sunnah say: If God willed, no polytheist would have associated partners with Him, no unbeliever would have disbelieved, and none of His creatures would have disobeyed Him. So how can what they claim be denied when it is true?

It is said: God denied them what they claimed to be the most lying and the most wicked of falsehoods. He did not deny them any truth or right. Rather, He denied them the most false of falsehoods. They did not mention what they mentioned in order to affirm His decree, His lordship, His oneness, their own need of Him, their reliance upon Him, and their seeking help from Him. Had they said it in that sense, they would have been correct. They said it only to oppose His law and to repel His command. Thus they opposed His law and command, and they rejected them by His decree and destiny. Everyone who opposes a command and rejects it by appealing to destiny agrees with them in this.

Furthermore, they argued from His general will and decree to His love for what He wills, His approval of it, and His permission for it. Thus they combined several kinds of error: opposing the command with destiny, repelling it by destiny, and reporting about God that He loves this from them and approves of it, since He willed and decreed it, and that they have a proof against the messengers through decree and destiny. Groups of people who claim realization and gnosis, or who claim it falsely, have inherited this error from them and followed them in it. They say: when the gnostic witnesses the divine judgment, blame falls away from him.

The words of Shaykh al-Islam Abu Isma'il Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari (may God have mercy on him) contain something that seems to suggest this, though God protects him from it. In the chapter on repentance in *Manazil al-sa'irin* (The Stations of Travelers), he said: "The subtleties of repentance are three.

The first: that we examine the offense and the decree, and recognize God's purpose in them: His letting you be and your committing them. God lets the servant and the sin alone for one of two reasons: that He may make His servant know His lesson in His decree, His goodness in His guidance, His forbearance in giving respite to the one who rides [sin], His generosity in accepting the servant's excuse, and His grace in forgiving him. The second is that He may establish against the servant the proof of His justice, so that He punishes him for his sin with His proof.

The second subtlety: to know that the seeking of the discerning sincere one does not leave him any good deed at all, since he travels between witnessing the favor (minnah) and seeking out the fault of the self and of the deed.

The third subtlety: the servant's witnessing of the judgment leaves him no appreciation of any good deed and no disapproval of any evil deed, because he has ascended from all meanings to the meaning of the judgment."

The apparent meaning of this last statement nullifies the appreciation of good and the disapproval of evil, yet all the sacred laws rest on the appreciation of this and the disapproval of that. Rather, witnessing the judgment increases the discerning one's appreciation of good and disapproval of evil. The more his knowledge of God, His names, His attributes, and His command grows, the stronger his appreciation and disapproval become, because in this he agrees with his Lord and His messengers, and with what the Most Beautiful Names and the Exalted Attributes require. Shaykh al-Islam was in this agreeing with the command, and his anger for God, for His limits, and for His prohibitions is well known among the elite and the common people. His earlier words clearly show the firmness of his stance in disapproving what God disapproved and approving what God approved. His words are clear (muhkam) in this, and this statement is ambiguous (mutashabih), so it must be referred back to his clear words.

What fits him best is what our shaykh Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Wasiti said in his commentary. He mentioned a principle concerning *fana'* (annihilation) and *istilam* (obliteration). He said: "Fana' is an expression for the servant's being overwhelmed (istilam) by the dominance of the Real's existence and the strength of the knowledge of Him in the servant. Through this his certainty and knowledge of Him and of His attributes increase, so he becomes stunned, just as a person is stunned by a great matter that has overtaken him. He may be absent from awareness of the important matters that overtook him, as when a man stands before a great, overpowering sovereign of the kings of the earth, and what he observes of the sovereign's awe and power distracts him from much of what he perceives. This is an approximation, and the reality is beyond it. How then about one whom God, the Mighty and Majestic, has made to witness His singularity (fardaniyyah), when there was nothing with Him? He sees things as dead, having no subsistence except through His power, and he witnesses them as an imagination, like dust, in relation to the existence of the Real, exalted is He. This occurs in the inner insight of the heart through sound unveiling, after purification and training in bearing the burdens of the Law, taking on its loads and adopting its character. God purifies His servant from his filth and unveils to his heart, so he sees the realities of things. When the lights of real, spiritual witnessing that indicate the greatness of singularity manifest upon the servant, the existence that belongs to the servant vanishes and dissolves, just as the night disappears when the morning brightens. The servant, in that state, eats and drinks, and nothing appears on him that differs from what he is accustomed to. Yet his faith and certainty increase, until his faith may cover everything in his heart during moments of intoxication (sukr). His existence remains like an imagination, standing in servanthood in the presence of the Lord of Majesty. Sound insights return to him in knowing things when he becomes sober (sahw). Then the lack of discernment (tamyiz) leaves him, and he becomes strong in his state and acts. This is *baqa'* (subsistence), by which he acts upon things, and what he found of faith and certainty in the state of subsistence is not veiled from him. Rather, his first awareness returns to him, with another existence that God, the Mighty and Majestic, takes charge of, and his witnessing of it is that God's standing over him is by His management. He reaches the station of the one who is willed (murad) after passing the station of the seeker (murid), so by Him he hears and by Him he speaks, as in the authentic hadith.

"Another aspect: the one who is annihilated in his state of fana', before he reaches subsistence, sobriety, and discernment, has his heart's place of asceticism (zuhd), patience (sabr), and scrupulousness (wara') covered over. This does not mean that those stations have gone and the servant has been lifted from them. It means that witnessing has covered their place in the heart, and they are folded and absorbed within what he has found, as a lower state is absorbed into a higher one. They become implicit and subordinate to what the finder has found of the existence of the Real. The heart becomes occupied with the higher state rather than the lower one. So if the servant's heart were searched, one would find within it asceticism, scrupulousness, and the realities of fear and hope hidden beneath mountain-like existential states, so that the heart cannot contain them all together. In the state of subsistence, sobriety, and discernment, those stations return to him through God, not through his own existence.

"If you know this, the problem in his statement that witnessing does not leave the servant any appreciation of a good deed or disapproval of an evil deed, because he has ascended to the meaning of the judgment, is resolved. That is, the attribute of God's judgment fills his insight and occupies it. He witnesses God's standing over things, His management of them, and His judgment upon them. He sees all things issuing from Him through the execution of His judgment, His decree, and His will in creation. Through his observation of this unity (jam'), he becomes absent from discernment (tamyiz) and distinction (farq). This is called *jam'* because the servant's gaze gathers upon his Master in every judgment that occurs in the cosmos. In contemplating this judgment from which the actions proceed, his heart gathers. Because his heart is weak at this gathering, it cannot contain the legal discernment between good and evil. That is, the judgment of his knowledge of good and evil is folded within this knowledge, which veils him from discernment. This does not mean that the judgment of approving and disapproving has been removed from his heart. Rather, it has been absorbed into his witnessing and folded within it, so that if one searched, one would find the judgment of approval and disapproval hidden within that witnessing." And success is from God.

The summary of what our shaykh (may God have mercy on him) mentioned is this: the act has two aspects. One aspect subsists in the Lord, the Exalted, namely His decree, His destiny, and His knowledge of it. The servant has two observations: an observation of the first aspect and an observation of the second. The perfection is that he is not absent from one observation by the other. Rather, he witnesses the Lord's decree, destiny, and will, and at the same time witnesses his own act, his sin, and his obedience or disobedience. Thus he witnesses both lordship and servanthood, and in his heart the meaning of God's words ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾ combines with His words ﴿And you will not, except that God wills﴾, and His words ﴿Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember, except that God wills﴾. Some people have hearts wide enough to contain these two witnessings. Others have hearts too narrow to combine them, because of the strength of what descends upon them and the weakness of the receptacle. Such a person is absent, through witnessing servanthood, acquisition (kasb), and the aspect of obedience and disobedience, from witnessing the judgment that subsists in the Lord, the Exalted, without denying it. Only the trace of the act and its legal judgment appears to him. This does not harm him as long as belief in the judgment remains established in his heart. Others are absent through witnessing the judgment, its precedence, and God's priority and precedence over things, away from the aspect of their own servanthood, acquisition, obedience, and disobedience. Through witnessing the judgment, they are absent from the one judged by it, let alone its attribute. When he does not witness the act itself, how could he witness it as good or evil? This also does not harm him, provided that his knowledge of the goodness and evil of the act remains in his heart. It is only hidden from him because the witnessing of the judgment has overpowered his heart. And success is from God.

How far is this from the argument of God's enemies, who use His will and decree to annul His command and prohibition? Their worshippers, these unbelievers, witness all their acts as acts of obedience, because they conform to the prior will. Yet if someone else angers them and falls short of their rights, they do not witness his act as obedience, even though it too conforms to the will. Whoever argues from destiny to nullify the command and prohibition is among the most ignorant and unjust of people, and the most devoted to his own desire. Reflect on His words, exalted is He, after relating what His enemies said, arguing with His will and decree to nullify what His messenger commanded them, and that were it not for His love and approval of it, He would not have willed it from them: ﴿Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾. He reports that the proof belongs to Him against them, through His messengers, His books, the clarification of what benefits and harms them, and His enabling them to believe by knowing His commands and prohibitions. He gave them hearing, sight, and intellect. Thus His conclusive proof is established against them, and their false proof against Him, through His will and decree, collapses. Then He confirmed the completeness of the proof with His words: ﴿So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾.

This implies that He alone is singular in lordship, dominion, and management of His creation, that there is no lord but Him and no god besides Him. How, then, could they worship another god along with Him? Affirming destiny and will is therefore part of His conclusive proof against them, and that all affairs belong to God, and that everything other than God is void. Destiny, decree, and the executing will are among the greatest proofs of monotheism. But the wrongdoers and deniers made them a proof for their polytheism. So God's proof is the conclusive one, and theirs is the refuted one. And success is from God.

Knowing this, Moses was too knowledgeable of God, His names, and His attributes to blame a man for a sin he repented of, after which his Lord chose him, guided him, and selected him. And Adam knew his Lord too well to argue from His decree and destiny for his disobedience. Rather, Moses only blamed Adam for the disobedience that reached his descendants when they were expelled from the Garden and sent down to the abode of trial and affliction, because of their father's error. Mentioning the error was a reminder of the cause of the calamity and affliction that befell the descendants. This is why Moses said to him, "You expelled us and yourself from the Garden," and in another wording, "You made us miserable."

So Adam argued from destiny against the calamity. He said that this calamity that befell the descendants because of my error had been written in His decree before I was created. Destiny may be invoked for calamities, but not for sins. That is: Would you blame me for a calamity that was decreed for me and for you before I was created, by so many years? This is the answer of our shaykh (may God have mercy on him). Another answer may also be suggested: arguing from destiny for a sin is beneficial in one situation and harmful in another. It is beneficial when one argues with it after the sin has occurred, and repents from it, and abandons repeating it, as Adam did. Then mentioning destiny at that point is part of monotheism and the knowledge of the Lord's names and attributes, and mentioning it benefits the one who recalls it and the one who hears it. It does not repel a command or a prohibition, nor does it annul the Law. Rather, it reports the pure truth in the manner of monotheism and disavowal of one's own power and strength.

This is clarified by the fact that Adam said to Moses, "Do you blame me for doing an act that was written against me before I was created?" When a man sins, then repents, and the matter is ended so that it is as though it had not happened, and then someone rebukes him and blames him for it, it is acceptable for him to argue from destiny afterward, saying, "This was a matter decreed against me before I was created." He has not used destiny to repel a right, nor mentioned it as a proof for falsehood, and there is no harm in arguing with it. The situation in which arguing with it is harmful is the present and the future: when one commits a forbidden act or abandons an obligation, and someone blames him for it, and he argues from destiny to justify it and persist in it. Then he annuls a right by this argument and commits falsehood, as those who insisted on their polytheism and worship of other than God argued, saying: ﴿If God had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers﴾, and ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾. They argued with it, justifying what they were doing, and they did not repent of their act, nor resolve to abandon it, nor acknowledge its corruption. This is the opposite of one who has realized the error of his own self, repented, and resolved with all determination never to return. If someone later blames him, he says, "What happened was by God's decree."

The crux of the matter is this: when blame is lifted, arguing from destiny is valid. When blame is actually present, arguing from destiny is invalid.

If it is said: Ali argued from destiny for abandoning night prayer, and the Prophet (ﷺ) approved it, as is in the authentic report from Ali: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to him and Fatimah at night and said to them, 'Will you not pray?' I said, 'O Messenger of God, our souls are in the hand of God. If He wills to raise them, He raises them.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned away when I said that and did not reply to me. Then I heard him as he was leaving, striking his thigh and saying: ﴿And man is ever most disputatious﴾."

It is answered: Ali did not argue from destiny to abandon an obligation or to commit a forbidden act. He only said that his soul and Fatimah's soul were in God's hand, so if He willed to wake them and raise their souls, He would raise them. This agrees with the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying on the night they slept in the valley: "God took our souls where He willed and returned them where He willed." This is a sound argument, and whoever makes it is excused, because the sleeper is not negligent. Arguing from destiny by one who is not negligent is valid. The Prophet (ﷺ) guided toward arguing from destiny in the situation where it benefits the servant. Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Hurayrah who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "The strong believer is better and more beloved to God than the weak believer. In everything there is good. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from God, and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, do not say, 'If only I had done such and such.' Rather, say, 'God decreed it, and He does what He wills,' for 'if only' opens the work of Satan."

This noble hadith contains great principles of faith. The first: God, glorified and exalted, is described as loving, and He truly loves. The second: He loves what the requirements of His names and attributes call for, and what agrees with them. He is the Strong, so He loves the strong believer. He is One and loves oneness (witr). He is Beautiful and loves beauty. He is Knowing and loves the knowledgeable. He is Pure and loves purity. He is Faithful and loves the faithful. He is the Doer of good and loves the doers of good. He is the Patient and loves the patient. He is the Grateful and loves the grateful.

Another principle: His love for believers varies, so He loves some of them more than others.

Another: a person's happiness lies in being eager for what benefits him in his livelihood and his hereafter. Eagerness is exerting effort and expending one's capacity. When the eager person hits upon what benefits him, his eagerness is praiseworthy. His perfection lies in combining two things: that he be eager, and that his eagerness be for what benefits him. If someone is eager for what does not benefit him, or does what benefits him without eagerness, he loses perfection in proportion to what he has missed. So all good lies in being eager for what benefits. Since a person's eagerness and actions occur only by God's help, will, and enabling, He commanded him to seek His help, so that the station of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ would be fulfilled in him. His eagerness for what benefits him is worship of God, and it is not complete except by His help. So He commanded him to worship Him and seek His help. Then He said, "Do not be incapable," because incapacity contradicts eagerness for what benefits him and contradicts seeking God's help. The one who is eager for what benefits him and seeks God's help is the opposite of the incapable. This is guidance before the decreed matter returns to what is among the greatest causes of its attainment, which is eagerness for it together with seeking help from the One in whose hand are the reins of affairs, from whom they proceed and to whom they return.

If something he was not decreed to obtain escapes him, he has two states. One is incapacity, which is the key to Satan's work. Incapacity leads him to "if only," and there is no benefit in "if only" here. It is rather the key to blame, distress, anger, regret, grief, and all of that is Satan's work. So the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade him to begin his work with this key, and commanded him to the second state, which is to look at destiny and observe it: that if it had been decreed for him, it would not have escaped him, and no one could have overpowered him in it. So there is nothing more beneficial for him here than witnessing destiny and the Lord's executing will, which necessitates the existence of what is decreed. When that will is absent, the existence of the decreed matter is impossible. This is why he said, "If something overcomes you, do not say, 'If only I had done such and such, it would have been so,' but say, 'God decreed it, and He does what He wills.'" Thus he guided him to what benefits him in both states: the state of attaining what he sought, and the state of its loss. Therefore this hadith is one that the servant can never do without. Rather, it is the most necessary thing for him. It contains the affirmation of destiny, acquisition, choice, standing, and servanthood, outwardly and inwardly, in both the state of attaining the desired thing and the state of its absence. And success is from God.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 20, verses 120–123 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" (120) So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden. Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. (121) Then his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him. (122) He said: "Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others. But when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer." (123)﴾

**(Benefit)**

**[Section: The difference between *ihtiyat* (caution) and *waswasa* (obsessive scrupulosity)]**

The difference between *ihtiyat* (precautionary caution) and *waswasa* (obsessive scrupulosity) is this: *ihtiyat* is thoroughness and earnestness in following the Sunnah and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions practised, without excess, transgression, negligence or neglect. This is the caution that Allah and His Messenger are pleased with. As for *waswasa*, it is the innovation of what the Sunnah has not brought and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and none of the Companions did, while claiming that by it one reaches the attainment and mastery of what is prescribed. Such a person, in his own view, is being cautious: he washes his limbs in wudu more than three times, so he wastes water in pouring it during his ablution and ritual bath; he repeatedly or once pronounces the intention for prayer aloud; he washes his clothes of what he is not certain is impure, out of caution; and he refrains from praying in his shoes, out of caution. These, and many times more than these, are what the obsessive have taken as religion, claiming them to be caution. Yet caution lies in following the guidance of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he practised, and that is more fitting for them, for it is the caution which whoever departs from has parted from caution and deviated from the even path. Complete caution lies in avoiding opposition to the Sunnah, even if one opposes most of the people of the earth, indeed all of them.

**(Subtle point)**

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then His Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him.﴾

The accursed one, out of his ignorance, supposed that Allah, glorified is He, would forsake His chosen and beloved, whom He created with His own hand, into whom He breathed of His spirit, to whom He caused His angels to prostrate, and whom He taught the names of all things, on account of a single meal he ate.

He did not know that a physician teaches the patient the remedy before the illness. When the patient feels the illness, he hastens to use the remedy. Likewise, when an enemy shoots him with an arrow that strikes not a fatal spot, he hastens to treat the wound, and he stands up as though no harm had befallen him.

The enemy was afflicted with sin, and he persisted, argued, opposed the command, found fault with the wisdom, did not ask for pardon, and did not repent of his lapse. The Beloved was afflicted with sin, and he acknowledged it, repented, was remorseful, humbled himself, submitted, and resorted to the refuge of creation, which is monotheism and seeking forgiveness. So the reproach was removed from him, his sin was forgiven, his repentance was accepted, and every door of mercy and guidance was opened to him. We are his children, and whoever resembles his father has not been wronged. Whoever's disposition is repentance and seeking forgiveness has been guided to the finest of dispositions.

**(Benefit)**

As for the Most High's words in Surah Taha: ﴿He said: "Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others."﴾ This is addressed to Adam and Eve.

Some scholars have said that the pronoun in His words ﴿Go down from it﴾ may refer either to Adam and his wife, or to Adam and Iblis. The wife is not mentioned because she follows him. On this view, the enmity mentioned is between the two addressed by the descent, namely Adam and Iblis, and the matter is clear.

On the first view, the verse contains two matters:

The first: His command, exalted is He, to Adam and his spouse to descend.

The second: His information about the enmity between Adam and his wife on one side and Iblis on the other. This is why the plural pronoun is used in the second matter and not in the first. It is certain that Iblis is included in the ruling of this enmity, as the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife﴾, and He said to the descendants: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾.

Reflect on how the passages mentioning enmity all use the plural pronoun rather than the dual.

As for the descent, He mentions it sometimes with the plural, sometimes with the dual, and sometimes with the singular, as in His words in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿He said: "Go down from it"﴾. Likewise in Surah Sad, and that was addressed to Iblis alone.

Wherever it occurs in the plural form, it addresses Adam, his wife and Iblis, since the story revolves around them. Wherever it occurs in the dual, it either addresses Adam and his wife, since they are the two who actually ate from the tree and committed the disobedience, or it addresses Adam and Iblis, since they are the fathers of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn) and the origins of the descendants. Thus their situation and the outcome of their affair are mentioned as an admonition and lesson for their offspring. Both views have been related.

What clarifies that the pronoun in His words ﴿Go down from it, all of you﴾ refers to Adam and Iblis is that when Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the disobedience, He singled out Adam without his wife, saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him. He said: "Go down from it, all of you"﴾.

This shows that the one addressed by the descent is Adam and the one who made disobedience appealing to him, and the wife entered as a follower. For the purpose is that Allah, exalted is He, informs the two weighty ones of what befell their two progenitors from the ill omen of disobedience and opposition to the command. Mentioning their two fathers conveys this meaning more forcefully than mentioning only the two fathers of mankind.

He, glorified is He, has informed us that the wife ate with Adam, and He informed us that He sent him down and expelled him from the Garden because of that eating. So it is known that the wife's ruling is the same and that she came to the same state as Adam. Directing attention to the situation of the two fathers of the two weighty ones is more fitting than directing it only to the father and mother of mankind. Reflect on this.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.﴾

He negated from him going astray, which is the torment of the heart and spirit, and suffering, which is the torment of the body and spirit as well. So he is granted delight of heart and body through guidance and success.

**(Benefit)**

Know that it has been established in His wisdom, glorified is He, that happiness, bliss and comfort are reached only over the bridge of hardship and fatigue, and entered only through the gate of hardships, patience and bearing toils. For this reason He surrounded Paradise with hardships and the Fire with desires. And for this reason He expelled His chosen, Adam, from Paradise, though He had created it for him. His wisdom required that he not enter it in a lasting entry except after toil and weariness. So He expelled him from it only so that He might admit him into it in the most complete entry.

How great is the difference between the first entry and the second entry! And how great is the difference between the Prophet's entry into Mecca under the protection of al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi and his entry into it on the day of the Conquest!

How great is the difference between the comfort and delight of the believers in Paradise after enduring what came before, and their delight had they been created in it!

How great is the difference between the joy of one whom He grants wellbeing after his trial, enriches after his poverty, guides after his straying, and gathers his heart after its dispersion, and the joy of one who has never tasted those bitternesses! The divine wisdom has already decreed that hardships are causes of pleasures and goods, as the Most High said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, and it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing which is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing which is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾

*A verse of poetry:*
"Often what is hateful to the souls becomes
the cause of what they love, and its like is no cause."

**(Section: On the mention of the dispute between Adam and Musa, peace be upon them)**

In this matter the Prophet (ﷺ) judged in favour of Adam, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

From Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Adam and Musa argued. Musa said: 'O Adam, you are our father; you made us miserable and expelled us from the Garden.' Adam said to him: 'You are Musa, whom Allah chose by His speech, and He inscribed the Torah for you with His own hand. Do you blame me for a matter that Allah decreed for me before He created me by forty years?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'So Adam won the argument over Musa, so Adam won the argument over Musa, so Adam won the argument over Musa.'"

In another narration: "He inscribed the Torah for you with His own hand."

In another wording: "Adam and Musa disputed. Musa said to him: 'You are Adam, whom you led people astray and expelled them from the Garden.' Adam said: 'You are Musa, whom Allah gave the knowledge of all things and chose above the people with His message.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you blame me for a matter that was decreed upon me before I was created?'"

In another wording: "Adam and Musa argued before their Lord. Adam won the argument over Musa. Musa said: 'You are Adam, whom Allah created with His hand, breathed into you of His spirit, caused His angels to prostrate to you, settled you in His Garden, then you caused the people to descend to the earth because of your sin.' Adam said: 'You are Musa, whom Allah chose with His message and His speech, gave you the tablets in which is the clarification of everything, and brought you near as a confidant. How much before my creation did you find Allah had written the Torah?' Musa said: 'Forty years.' Adam said: 'Did you find in it: "And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray"?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you blame me for doing an action that Allah wrote that I should do before He created me by forty years?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'So Adam won the argument over Musa.'"

In another wording: "Adam and Musa argued. Musa said to him: 'You are the one whose sin expelled us from the Garden.'" And he mentioned the hadith...

It is agreed upon as authentic, and this determination occurred after the earlier determination mentioned before, by fifty thousand years before the creation of the heavens.

The Mu'tazilites who failed to understand this hadith rejected it, such as Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i and those who agreed with him. He said: "If it were authentic, the prophethoods of the prophets would be invalidated, for if predestination were a proof for the disobedient, the command and prohibition would be void. For the one who disobeys by abandoning a command or committing a prohibition, if the argument from predestination is valid for him, blame is lifted from him."

This is from the error of the Mu'tazilite group and their ignorance of Allah, His Messenger and his Sunnah. This is an authentic hadith, agreed upon as authentic, which the Umma has never ceased to receive with acceptance from the time of its Prophet, generation after generation, meeting it with affirmation and submission. The people of hadith recorded it in their books and bore witness that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it, and they judged it authentic. What then is the matter with those most ignorant of the Sunnah, and those known for their enmity to it and to its bearers, and for testifying against them that they are anthropomorphists, likeners and literalist filler-transmitters? This has been the way of the people of false kalam (theology), who have always been charged with rejecting the hadiths of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that contradict their false principles and corrupt creeds. They rejected the hadiths of the vision (of Allah), the hadiths of Allah's elevation above His creation, the hadiths of His attributes subsisting in Him, the hadiths of intercession, the hadiths of His descent to the lowest heaven, His descent to the earth to judge between His servants, the hadiths of His speaking by revelation as real speech that whomever He wills of His creation hears, and similar matters. Likewise the Kharijites and Mu'tazilites rejected the hadiths about the emergence of the people of major sins from the Fire through intercession and other things. The Rafidites rejected the hadiths about the virtues of the rightly-guided Caliphs and other Companions. The Mu'attilah (deniers of attributes) rejected the hadiths of the attributes and voluntary actions. The Qadariyyah, who are the Magians of this Umma, rejected the hadiths of decree and predestination. Every one who established a principle that Allah and His Messenger did not establish has been driven by compulsion to reject the Sunnah and distort it from its proper places. Therefore the party of Allah and His Messenger has established no principle other than what the Messenger brought. It is their foundation upon which they rely, and their paradise to which they return.

Then people differed in understanding this hadith and the aspect of the argument by which Adam prevailed over Musa.

One group said: "He prevailed over him only because Adam was his father, so he prevailed over him as a man prevails over his son." This statement has no substance whatsoever, for Allah's proof must be turned to whether the one involved is a father or a son, a slave or a master. Even if a man prevails over his father with a true proof, it is obligatory to yield to the proof.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because the sin was under one law and the blame under another law."

This is of the same type as the previous view, for this has no influence on the argument in any way. This Umma blames the nations that opposed their earlier messengers, even though they did not share one law, and Allah accepts their testimony against them even though they were not people of the same law.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because he had repented of the sin, and the one who has repented of sin is like one who has no sin, and it is not permissible to blame him." Although this is closer than what preceded it, it is not valid, for three reasons:

First: Adam did not mention this aspect, nor did he make it a proof against Musa. He did not say: "Do you blame me for a sin from which I have repented?"

Second: Musa knows Allah, glorified is He, and His command and religion better than to blame a sin about which Allah informed him that He had forgiven its doer, chose him afterwards, and guided him. This is not permissible even for ordinary believers, let alone the interlocutor of the Most Merciful.

Third: This would entail nullifying what the Prophet (ﷺ) attached as the aspect of the argument, and taking into account what he set aside, which should not be considered.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because Musa blamed him in a realm that is not the abode of obligation. If he had blamed him in the abode of obligation, the argument would have been Musa's." This too is invalid for two reasons:

First: Adam did not say to him: "You blamed me in a realm that is not the abode of obligation." He said only: "Do you blame me for a matter decreed for me before I was created?" He did not address the realm; he argued from the prior decree.

Second: Allah, glorified is He, blames the blameworthy among His servants in a realm that is not the abode of obligation. He blames them after death and blames them on the Day of Resurrection.

Another group said: "He prevailed over him only because Adam witnessed the divine judgment and its operation over creation, and the Lord's sole lordship, and that not a particle moves except by His will and knowledge, that none can repel His decree and destiny, and that what He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be." They said: "The servant's witnessing of the judgment leaves him no room to find any evil reprehensible, for he sees himself as pure nonexistence, the judgments operate upon him, he knows them, and he is subjugated, a created and managed being with no strategy and no power. Whoever witnesses this station is relieved of blame." This path is the most corrupt path that has been taken in this hadith, and it is worse than the path of the Qadariyyah in rejecting it. They rejected it only to refute this claim and to answer its proponents. They were right in their refutation of these people and in demolishing their claim, but they erred in rejecting the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For if this path were valid, all religions would be nullified altogether, predestination would become a proof for every polytheist, disbeliever and wrongdoer, the prescribed punishments would have no meaning, no criminal would be blamed for his crime, no wrongdoer for his wrongdoing, and no one would ever forbid wrongdoing.

For this reason the shaykh of the heretics, Ibn Sina, said in his *Isharat*: "The gnostic does not forbid wrongdoing, because he has insight into the secret of Allah in predestination." This is words stripped of religion and of following the messengers. Allah's most knowing creatures of Him are His messengers and prophets, and they are the greatest of people in forbidding wrongdoing. They were sent only to forbid wrongdoing. So the gnostic is the greatest of people in forbidding wrongdoing, because of his insight into the command and the decree. The command obliges him to forbid, and the decree helps him in it and enacts it for him. So he stands in the station of "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help" and in the station of "So worship Him and rely upon Him." We worship Him by His command and His decree, and we rely on Him in executing His command by His decree. This is the reality of knowledge, and the possessor of this station is the gnostic of Allah. Upon this all the messengers agreed, from the first to the last.

As for the one who says:
"I have become one acted upon by what He chooses from me, so my every act is obedience,"
and who says: "Even if I disobey His command, I have obeyed His will and His wish," and who says: "The gnostic does not forbid wrongdoing, because of his insight into Allah's secret in predestination," such a person has departed from what all the messengers were upon, and he is not among their followers. Allah, glorified is He, related the argument from predestination of the polytheists, the enemies of the messengers, saying: ﴿Those who associated partners with Allah will say: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers"﴾ up to His words: ﴿Say: "Then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof. So had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ And He said: ﴿Those who associated partners said: "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, we or our fathers"﴾ up to His words: ﴿So is there upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ And He said: ﴿And when it is said to them: "Spend from what Allah has provided you," those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?"﴾ And He said: ﴿And they say: "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾

These are four places in which the argument from predestination is related from His enemies. Their shaykh and imam in this was their most despicable enemy, Iblis, who argued against Allah by His decree, saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make [evil] attractive to them upon the earth and will mislead them all."﴾

If it is said: The texts and reason have established the truth of their words, "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor our fathers," and "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him," and "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them," for what Allah wills comes to be and what He does not will does not come to be. And the Most High said: ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾, and He said: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾.

Then how could I call them liars, when He denied them knowledge and affirmed that they were only guessing, while they are truthful in what they claim? All the People of the Sunnah say: If God willed, no polytheist would have associated partners with Him, no unbeliever would have disbelieved, and none of His creatures would have disobeyed Him. So how can what they claim be denied when it is true?

It is said: God denied them what they claimed to be the most lying and the most wicked of falsehoods. He did not deny them any truth or right. Rather, He denied them the most false of falsehoods. They did not mention what they mentioned in order to affirm His decree, His lordship, His oneness, their own need of Him, their reliance upon Him, and their seeking help from Him. Had they said it in that sense, they would have been correct. They said it only to oppose His law and to repel His command. Thus they opposed His law and command, and they rejected them by His decree and destiny. Everyone who opposes a command and rejects it by appealing to destiny agrees with them in this.

Furthermore, they argued from His general will and decree to His love for what He wills, His approval of it, and His permission for it. Thus they combined several kinds of error: opposing the command with destiny, repelling it by destiny, and reporting about God that He loves this from them and approves of it, since He willed and decreed it, and that they have a proof against the messengers through decree and destiny. Groups of people who claim realization and gnosis, or who claim it falsely, have inherited this error from them and followed them in it. They say: when the gnostic witnesses the divine judgment, blame falls away from him.

The words of Shaykh al-Islam Abu Isma'il Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari (may God have mercy on him) contain something that seems to suggest this, though God protects him from it. In the chapter on repentance in *Manazil al-sa'irin* (The Stations of Travelers), he said: "The subtleties of repentance are three.

The first: that we examine the offense and the decree, and recognize God's purpose in them: His letting you be and your committing them. God lets the servant and the sin alone for one of two reasons: that He may make His servant know His lesson in His decree, His goodness in His guidance, His forbearance in giving respite to the one who rides [sin], His generosity in accepting the servant's excuse, and His grace in forgiving him. The second is that He may establish against the servant the proof of His justice, so that He punishes him for his sin with His proof.

The second subtlety: to know that the seeking of the discerning sincere one does not leave him any good deed at all, since he travels between witnessing the favor (minnah) and seeking out the fault of the self and of the deed.

The third subtlety: the servant's witnessing of the judgment leaves him no appreciation of any good deed and no disapproval of any evil deed, because he has ascended from all meanings to the meaning of the judgment."

The apparent meaning of this last statement nullifies the appreciation of good and the disapproval of evil, yet all the sacred laws rest on the appreciation of this and the disapproval of that. Rather, witnessing the judgment increases the discerning one's appreciation of good and disapproval of evil.
